Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On October 12, 2023, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced the rollout of two highly requested features for the Threads platform: an edit button and 'Voice Threads'. The edit functionality allows users to modify their posts for up to five minutes after publishing. Edited posts display an icon to indicate a change has been made, but an edit history showing previous versions is not available. The second feature, Voice Threads, enables users to record and share audio messages directly in a thread, which are then automatically transcribed. These updates, provided free of charge, were part of Meta's ongoing efforts to enhance the app's functionality and user experience following its initial launch. <2> Meta Platforms, in partnership with EssilorLuxottica, announced the next-generation Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses on September 27, 2023, during the annual Meta Connect event. [1, 2] The new collection introduced several key upgrades, including an improved 12 MP ultra-wide camera for higher-quality photos and 1080p videos, and for the first time, the ability to livestream directly to Facebook and Instagram for up to 30 minutes. [1, 9] The glasses also feature a five-microphone array and improved open-ear speakers with enhanced bass and noise suppression. [1] A major addition is the integration of Meta AI, the company's conversational assistant, which can be activated with the voice prompt "Hey Meta" for a hands-free experience (initially launched as a beta feature in the U.S.). [1, 9] The glasses, powered by the Qualcomm Snapdragon AR1 Gen1 Platform, are available in the classic Wayfarer design and a new Headliner style, with over 150 custom frame and lens combinations. [2, 9] Starting at a price of $299, pre-orders for the Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses began on the announcement date, September 27, 2023, with general retail availability starting on October 17, 2023. [7, 9] <3> At its two-day Connect 2023 conference on September 27, 2023, Meta announced the introduction of Meta AI, an advanced conversational assistant. The AI began rolling out in beta in the United States and is integrated into WhatsApp, Messenger, and Instagram. It is also slated for inclusion in the Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses and the Quest 3 headset. This new assistant is powered by a custom model that utilizes Llama 2 technology and can access real-time information through a partnership with Microsoft's Bing search engine. Concurrently, Meta also launched 28 other AI characters, each with a unique personality, with some being voiced by celebrities such as Snoop Dogg, Tom Brady, and Kendall Jenner. <4> At its Connect 2023 conference on September 27, 2023, Meta announced and released a new suite of 28 AI-powered chatbots in beta for its messaging apps, including WhatsApp, Messenger, and Instagram. [1, 2, 6] Initially made available to a select group of users in the U.S., these chatbots feature distinct personas, with some embodied by cultural icons and influencers such as Snoop Dogg, Tom Brady, and Kendall Jenner. [6] It was clarified that these AIs do not replicate the celebrities' actual personalities but rather assume fictional roles; for instance, the Snoop Dogg chatbot acts as a "Dungeon Master" and the Tom Brady bot is a sports debater named "Bru." <5> Meta officially launched the Meta Quest 3, a mixed reality headset, during the Meta Connect 2023 conference on September 27, 2023. The company, which touted the device as the first mainstream mixed-reality headset, announced that pre-orders were available immediately following the presentation. The headset was scheduled to begin shipping to customers on October 10, 2023. While an initial teaser and price point were revealed on June 1, 2023, the full launch details, pre-order information, and event took place in September. <6> On August 1, 2023, Meta began permanently ending the availability of news content on its Facebook and Instagram platforms for all users in Canada. [1, 4] This action, which was rolled out over the subsequent weeks, prevents people in Canada from viewing or sharing news links and content from both Canadian and international news outlets. [2, 3] The move was a direct response to Canada's Online News Act (Bill C-18), which passed on June 22, 2023, and would require tech giants like Meta to negotiate payments to news publishers for their content. [3, 9] Meta stated that the legislation is based on the "incorrect premise that Meta benefits unfairly from news content shared on our platforms, when the reverse is true". [2] In contrast, Canadian Heritage Minister Pascale St-Onge called the action "irresponsible," and CBC/Radio-Canada described it as an "abuse of their market power". [4, 5] <7> Meta announced the public release of Llama 2, its next-generation open-source large language model, on July 18, 2023, making it available for both research and commercial use. [2, 3, 4] This was a significant step in Meta's focus on advancing AI, with the company stating they believe an open approach is crucial for the development of current AI models. [4] Llama 2 was released in partnership with Microsoft, which was named the preferred partner for the model. [2, 4] The model is accessible through platforms like Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Hugging Face. [4, 5] Llama 2 was trained on 40% more public data than its predecessor and can process a larger context. [3] The release includes pretrained and fine-tuned versions, known as Llama-2-Chat, which are optimized for dialogue and range from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters. [6] While Llama 2 models show strong performance against other open-source models, they are comparable to some closed-source models like ChatGPT. [5, 6] <8> Norway's data protection authority, Datatilsynet, announced on July 17, 2023, that it was imposing a temporary ban on Meta from using behavioral advertising on its Facebook and Instagram platforms within the country. The authority deemed Meta's practice of monitoring user activity—such as location, content preferences, and posts—for marketing purposes to be illegal. The three-month ban officially commenced on August 4, 2023. To enforce the ban, a daily fine of 1 million Norwegian kroner (approximately $98,500) was set to be levied starting August 14, 2023, for non-compliance. This action followed a July 4, 2023, decision by the Court of Justice of the European Union, which found Meta's data collection for advertising to be unlawful. In September 2023, Datatilsynet requested that the European Data Protection Board (EDPB) make the ban permanent and extend it to the entire European Economic Area. <9> Meta announced and launched Meta Quest+, a new virtual reality subscription service, on June 26, 2023. The service is available for Meta Quest 2, Meta Quest Pro, and is forward-compatible with the Quest 3. For a monthly fee of $7.99 or an annual fee of $59.99, subscribers receive access to two curated VR titles each month. Users retain access to the games as long as their subscription is active, and an introductory offer allowed new users to sign up for $1 for the first month. The launch titles for July were 'Pistol Whip' and 'Pixel Ripped 1995', with 'Walkabout Mini Golf' and 'Mothergunship: Forge' announced for August. <10> Meta's annual conference, Meta Connect, took place on September 27 and 28, 2023. The event, which was a return to an in-person format, featured significant announcements regarding the company's advancements in mixed reality, virtual reality, and artificial intelligence. The keynote address by CEO Mark Zuckerberg included the full unveiling of the Meta Quest 3 headset, a mixed reality device featuring full-color passthrough. Other major announcements included the next generation of Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, the integration of Xbox Cloud Gaming into Quest devices starting in December, and a suite of new AI-powered experiences and chatbots for Meta's messaging platforms.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On November 8, 2023, Meta announced a new global policy requiring political, electoral, and social issue advertisers to disclose when an ad has been created or altered using AI or other digital methods. The policy, which was set to take effect in January 2024, applies to content that realistically depicts people who do not exist, portrays real people saying or doing things they did not, or shows events that did not happen. This move is part of a broader effort by tech companies to address the potential for AI-generated content to mislead voters ahead of major elections. Meta will add labels to these ads to inform viewers, and failure to disclose may result in the ad's rejection. <2> Arturo Béjar, a former engineering director for Facebook's 'Protect & Care' team, testified before the U.S. Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Privacy, Technology, and the Law on November 7, 2023. [1] Béjar's concerns were personally motivated by his own daughter's experiences with repeated unwanted sexual advances and harassment on Instagram, which he said the company did nothing about after she reported the incidents. [5, 8] In an October 2021 email to Zuckerberg and other executives, Béjar had detailed a 'critical gap' between Meta's approach to harm and the reality of user experiences. [2, 6] During his testimony, he cited internal company data showing that in a single week, 13% of teen Instagram users aged 13 to 15 reported receiving unwanted sexual advances. [1] He accused Meta of providing 'placebo' safety tools and claimed that more effective tools he had helped build during his earlier tenure at Facebook had since been removed. [9, 11] While testing and the onboarding of contributors started in March, the formal end of the prior fact-checking program and the first public appearance of notes on the platforms commenced on April 7, 2025. As part of this transparency update, Meta disclosed that it sent over 2 million CyberTip reports concerning child sexual exploitation on Facebook, Instagram, and Threads to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) during Q4 2024. Of these reports, over 150,000 involved inappropriate interactions with children, while over 1.8 million were related to shared or re-shared photos and videos containing child sexual abuse material (CSAM). <7> Meta has officially announced its 2025 Connect conference, scheduled to take place from September 17-18, 2025. The event will be livestreamed and will showcase the company's latest developments in AR, VR, wearables, and the metaverse. In a change from previous years, dedicated AI announcements, particularly concerning the Llama models, will be featured at a separate, inaugural 'LlamaCon' event on April 29, 2025. At Connect, Meta is expected to provide updates on Meta Horizon, developer tools for the XR platform, and future technologies. Meta's CTO, Andrew Bosworth, has hinted at significant announcements related to wearables and metaverse software during the conference. <8> Meta hosted its first-ever LlamaCon, a virtual developer conference, on April 29, 2025, dedicated to its open-source Llama AI models and tools. The event aimed to share the latest developments in Meta's open-source AI community and guide developers on building and integrating AI-powered applications. Key moments included a keynote address and discussions featuring Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg in conversation with Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella about the future of AI. The conference also offered a glimpse at upcoming AI features and updates to the Llama collection of models, following the recent release of the Llama 4 family of models.
